title: Cohen power series presentation of a complete local ring
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] local ring which is $\mathfrak m$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], and put $k=A/\mathfrak m$. Then there are an integer $n\ge0$, a field $\Lambda$ when $\operatorname{char}(k)=0$ or a Cohen ring $\Lambda$ with maximal ideal $p\Lambda$ when $\operatorname{char}(k)=p>0$ [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring], and a surjective local homomorphism $q: R=\Lambda[[X_1,\ldots,X_n]]\to A$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. The induced map $R/\mathfrak m_R\to k$ is an isomorphism. In the field case $\Lambda\to k$ is an isomorphism; in the Cohen case $\Lambda/p\Lambda\to k$ is an isomorphism. In the field case the images of the $X_i$ generate $\mathfrak m$; in the Cohen case the images of $p,X_1,\ldots,X_n$ generate $\mathfrak m$. The ring $R$ is a complete Noetherian regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme] with parameters $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ in the field case and $p,X_1,\ldots,X_n$ in the Cohen case.

source.place: Algebra, Theorem Tag 032A (theorem-cohen-structure-theorem), part (2) and final paragraph of proof; Remark Tag 032C (remark-Noetherian-complete-local-ring-universally-catenary) for regularity of the power series ring. The residue-field isomorphism follows from the coefficient-ring property in part (1).

proof.text: (The surjection.) $A$ is Noetherian, so its maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ is finitely generated, and $A$ is $\mathfrak m$-adically complete. Let $p\ge0$ be the characteristic of $k=A/\mathfrak m$. By [lem-weil-pbc-cohen-structure-power-series-surjection] there are $n\ge0$, a ring $\Lambda$ which is a field of characteristic $0$ if $p=0$ and a Cohen ring [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring] with residue characteristic $p$ if $p>0$ (a discrete valuation ring with maximal ideal $p\Lambda$, $p\Lambda$-adically complete), and a surjective ring homomorphism $q:R=\Lambda[[X_1,\ldots,X_n]]\to A$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. (The clauses below are derived from the statement of that node alone, for every surjection $q$ of this form; how $q$ is built is not used.) Write $\mathfrak m_\Lambda$ for the maximal ideal of $\Lambda$: $\mathfrak m_\Lambda=0$ in the field case, $\mathfrak m_\Lambda=p\Lambda$ in the Cohen case.

source.place: Algebra, Theorem Tag 032A (theorem-cohen-structure-theorem, line 44929), part (2) and the last paragraph of the proof ('if $y_1,\ldots,y_n$ are generators of the ideal $\mathfrak m$ ... this map is surjective')

proof.text: (The ring $R$.) By [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-field-cohen-regular-complete] applied to $\Lambda$ and $d=n$: (1) $R$ is a Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] local domain with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_R=(X_1,\ldots,X_n)$ in the field case and $\mathfrak m_R=(p,X_1,\ldots,X_n)$ in the Cohen case; (2) the composite $\Lambda\to R\to R/\mathfrak m_R$ induces an isomorphism $\Lambda/\mathfrak m_\Lambda\xrightarrow{\sim}R/\mathfrak m_R$; (3) $R$ is $\mathfrak m_R$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]; (4) $R$ is a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme] of Krull dimension [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] $n$ in the field case and $n+1$ in the Cohen case.

source.place: Algebra, Remark Tag 032C (remark-Noetherian-complete-local-ring-universally-catenary, line 45023) (stated there without proof; proved in the cited node)

proof.text: ($q$ is local and $q(\mathfrak m_R)=\mathfrak m$.) Let $\mathfrak p=q^{-1}(\mathfrak m)$. Since $q$ is surjective, $\bar q:R\to A\to A/\mathfrak m=k$ is surjective with kernel $\mathfrak p$, so $R/\mathfrak p\cong k$ is a field and $\mathfrak p$ is a maximal ideal of $R$. As $R$ is local (step 2), $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak m_R$. Hence $q(\mathfrak m_R)\subseteq\mathfrak m$, i.e. $q$ is a local homomorphism; and since $q$ is surjective, $q(\mathfrak m_R)=q(q^{-1}(\mathfrak m))=\mathfrak m$.

source.place: Algebra, Theorem Tag 032A (theorem-cohen-structure-theorem, line 44929), part (2) (the clause 'local' is left implicit in Stacks; written out here)

proof.text: (Residue isomorphisms.) By step 3, $q$ induces $\bar q:R/\mathfrak m_R\to A/\mathfrak m=k$, $F\bmod\mathfrak m_R\mapsto q(F)\bmod\mathfrak m$; it is surjective since $q$ is, and its kernel is $q^{-1}(\mathfrak m)/\mathfrak m_R=\mathfrak m_R/\mathfrak m_R=0$; so $R/\mathfrak m_R\to k$ is an isomorphism. Composing with the isomorphism $\Lambda/\mathfrak m_\Lambda\xrightarrow{\sim}R/\mathfrak m_R$ of step 2 (2), the map $\Lambda/\mathfrak m_\Lambda\to k$, $\lambda\bmod\mathfrak m_\Lambda\mapsto q(\lambda)\bmod\mathfrak m$, is an isomorphism: in the field case $\mathfrak m_\Lambda=0$ and $\Lambda\to k$ is an isomorphism; in the Cohen case $\mathfrak m_\Lambda=p\Lambda$ and $\Lambda/p\Lambda\to k$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Algebra, Theorem Tag 032A (theorem-cohen-structure-theorem, line 44929), proof, last paragraph ('surjective modulo $(x_1,\ldots,x_n)$ by construction'): the residue isomorphisms, written out here

proof.text: (Generators of $\mathfrak m$.) For a surjective ring homomorphism $q$ and an ideal $I=(s_1,\ldots,s_r)$ of $R$, $q(I)=\{\sum q(c_i)q(s_i)\}=\{\sum a_iq(s_i):a_i\in A\}$ is the ideal $(q(s_1),\ldots,q(s_r))$ of $A$, since every $a_i$ is some $q(c_i)$. Apply this to $I=\mathfrak m_R$ with the generators of step 2 (1), and use $q(\mathfrak m_R)=\mathfrak m$ (step 3): in the field case $\mathfrak m$ is generated by $q(X_1),\ldots,q(X_n)$; in the Cohen case by $q(p)=p\cdot1_A,q(X_1),\ldots,q(X_n)$.

source.place: Algebra, Theorem Tag 032A (theorem-cohen-structure-theorem, line 44929), proof, last paragraph ('$x_i\mapsto y_i$' with $y_1,\ldots,y_n$ generators of $\mathfrak m$)

proof.text: ($R$ complete regular with its parameters.) By step 2, $R$ is Noetherian, local and $\mathfrak m_R$-adically complete, and it is a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme]: its maximal ideal is generated by $\dim R$ elements. Explicitly, in the field case $\dim R=n$ and $\mathfrak m_R$ is generated by the $n$ elements $X_1,\ldots,X_n$; in the Cohen case $\dim R=n+1$ and $\mathfrak m_R$ is generated by the $n+1$ elements $p,X_1,\ldots,X_n$. So these elements are a set of $\dim R$ generators of $\mathfrak m_R$, i.e. a regular system of parameters of $R$, which is what 'with parameters' means in the statement.

lean.statement: theorem cohen_power_series_presentation (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A] [IsAdicComplete (maximalIdeal A) A] : ∃ (n : ℕ) (Λ : Type u) (_ : CommRing Λ) (_ : IsLocalRing Λ) (_ : IsRegularLocalRing (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) Λ)), IsAdicComplete (maximalIdeal (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) Λ)) (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) Λ) ∧ ∃ q : MvPowerSeries (Fin n) Λ →+* A, Function.Surjective q ∧ IsLocalHom q ∧ (∃ e : ResidueField (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) Λ) ≃+* ResidueField A, ∀ f, e (residue (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) Λ) f) = residue A (q f)) ∧ ((IsField Λ ∧ CharZero (ResidueField A) ∧ (∃ e : Λ ≃+* ResidueField A, ∀ a, e a = residue A (q (MvPowerSeries.C a))) ∧ Ideal.span (Set.range (fun i : Fin n ↦ q (MvPowerSeries.X i))) = maximalIdeal A ∧ IsRegularSystemOfParameters (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n ↦ (MvPowerSeries.X i : MvPowerSeries (Fin n) Λ)))) ∨ (∃ p : ℕ, CharP (ResidueField A) p ∧ IsCohenRing p Λ ∧ (∃ e : (Λ ⧸ Ideal.span {(p : Λ)}) ≃+* ResidueField A, ∀ a, e (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ a) = residue A (q (MvPowerSeries.C a))) ∧ Ideal.span (insert (q (MvPowerSeries.C (p : Λ))) (Set.range (fun i : Fin n ↦ q (MvPowerSeries.X i)))) = maximalIdeal A ∧ IsRegularSystemOfParameters (MvPowerSeries.C (p : Λ) :: List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n ↦ (MvPowerSeries.X i : MvPowerSeries (Fin n) Λ)))))
